scenes.line1: How does Spark handle real-time data?
scenes.say: How does Spark handle data that never stops coming in? Is it streaming, batch, or both?

scenes.label: Streams
scenes.sub: Structured Streaming treats streams as unbounded tables.
scenes.say: With Structured Streaming, Spark treats a stream like an endless table. Data keeps arriving, and Spark keeps processing.

rows.b: Process data by actual event time

scenes.say: You get the familiar DataFrame API, event-time processing for accuracy, and stateful operations like running counts or windowed aggregations.

scenes.title: Read from Kafka, write to sink
scenes.say: For example, you can read from Kafka and write results to a sink, all in real time.

scenes.label: Exactly-once
scenes.sub: Use watermarking and checkpointing for safety.
scenes.say: To make sure you never lose or double process data, use watermarking for late events and checkpointing for recovery.

scenes.question: Is Structured Streaming just batch in disguise?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it just runs batches on streams.
scenes.right: No, it processes unbounded data, supports event-time, and does stateful ops.
scenes.say: Careful—Structured Streaming isn't just batch jobs on a loop. It handles unbounded data, tracks event time, and manages state for real-time needs.
